title: Exact Analytic, Geometric, Partition, and Slice Rank Separations over Finite Fields
abstract: We establish three exact, closed-form separation theorems linking analytic rank (ar), geometric rank (gr), partition rank (pr), and slice rank (sr) of structured multilinear tensors over finite fields F_p. First, on the complete 3-uniform hypergraph tensor K_n^(3)(x,y,z) = sum_{i,j,k distinct} x_i y_j z_k, we prove an unbounded characteristic-2 vs. odd-characteristic phase transition: over F_2, sr_{F_2}(K_n^(3)) = 3 for all n >= 3, and every slice matrix M_x has rank in the exact three-value set {0, 2, 2*floor((n-1)/2)}, yielding the exact closed-form bias bias_{F_2}(K_n^(3)) = 1/8 + 7 / 2^(2*floor((n-1)/2) + 3) and ar_{F_2}(K_n^(3)) < 3 uniformly; over every odd prime p >= 3, however, sr_{F_p}(K_n^(3)) >= n - 3 grows linearly, with exact bias_{F_3}(K_6^(3)) = 8821/531441 (ar_{F_3} = 3.7306 > 3). Second, we derive universal closed-form bias formulas for the 3x3 determinant tensor (bias_{F_p}(det_3) = p^(-2) + p^(-3) - p^(-5), certifying strict three-way separation ar_{F_2}(det_3) = log_2(32/11) < 2 = gr(det_3) < 3 = sr(det_3) via a 4-line cross-product proof over every field) and for general n x n matrix multiplication M_n via q-binomial matrix counts (explicitly bias_{F_p}(M_2) = (p^4 + 3p^3 - 2p^2 - 2p + 1)/p^7, certifying strict finite-field deficit ar_{F_p}(M_n) < gr(M_n) = ceil(3n^2/4) for all p and n >= 2 with lim_{p->inf} ar_{F_p}(M_n) = ceil(3n^2/4)), complemented by a complete zero-float contraction-rank atlas of alternating 3-forms in Lambda^3(F_2^n) distinguishing the G_2 Fano 3-form (bias 29/512) from the rank-2-free maximal 7-dimensional 3-form (bias 95/2048). Third, on the balanced 2m-tensor T_d^(2m) = prod_{j=1}^m <x^(j), y^(j)>, we prove over every field and every d >= 2, m >= 2 the exact unbounded separation ar_{F_p}(T_d^(2m)) < 1 = pr(T_d^(2m)) < d = sr(T_d^(2m)) via a 3-line I_{d^m}-flattening bound and exact closed-form bias 1 - ((p-1)/p)^(m-1)(1 - p^(-d))^m. A two-layer verification artifact accompanies the paper: 20 constructive, axiom-free Lean 4.36.0 theorems formalizing the closed-form bias, q-binomial exponent, and flattening kernel, paired with 16 zero-float Python certificates and 56 adversarial tests.
